rationale: Evidence: iteration 5 (sensors moved to y 0.06, kp 4.0, ki 0.3, kd 0.25, base_speed 1.3) is the best raced design at 84.33, up from 74.19. Every trial on all three tracks still went off track with one line-loss event per run. max_error stayed at 0.0617 to 0.0654 m, so the off-track floor has not moved across iterations 0 to 5 whatever the gains or the sensor y. The oval steering_oscillation of 0.244 is close to the 0.25 return threshold, and the s-bend is at 0.204. Progress is still low (oval 0.35, s-bend 0.17, slalom 0.09), so base_speed is not yet the binding limit. Raising base_speed now would only make the drift worse. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), which cannot exceed 0.06 within the allowed body_width range, so widening the body does not help. The Evaluator's stated next lever is sensor_size, and this change is a single-variable test. Change: sensor_size goes from 0.012 to 0.016 m, with all sensor positions (y 0.06, x -0.04 to 0.04), weights and controller values held at iteration 5. The larger footprint should give each sensor a smoother, more graded reading near the tape edge and reduce the chance of a total line loss on sharp bends. Expected result: line_loss_events fall on some seeds and max_error moves below about 0.062 m. This is uncertain. If max_error stays at 0.062 to 0.065 m, the floor is not from the sensor footprint and the next test is a narrower or wider x spread. If the score falls below 84.33 or oscillation exceeds 0.25 on the oval, revert to sensor_size 0.012 and try kd 0.3 with kp 4.0. Do not raise base_speed until progress nears 0.995 with no line loss. Completion within 3 s is not expected at base_speed 1.3.
